newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 5.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 5.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - A top executive at Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS television unit says he expects the division to sell about $540 million in advertising for its broadcast of the 1998 Winter Olympics in Hagano, Japan, about 50 percent above sales during the 1994 winter games.

PARIS - France has football fever 10 months before it hosts the World Cup tournament next June, and advertisers linked with the event are getting in early on the act. Oil firm Total, the offical oil company for the World Cup, is setting out to be the first with World Cup clothes and accessories on sale, says Alain Castinel, Total's head of advertising and promotion.
LONDON - Income at Britain's advertising agencies has been rising, but profitability remains stagnant and there has been little increase in productivity, an advertising accountancy firm reports.

LONDON - Bell's whisky says it will launch a four million pound ($6.5 million) advertising campaign for its eight-year-old Scotch whisky that is designed to maintain its leading market share in Britain.

DUESSELDORF - More than every tenth mark spent on advertising goes towards promotional goods, says the Association of Promotional Goods. Turnover for 1997 will reach six billion marks ($3.2 billion), up from 5.7 billion marks in 1996, the association says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PALO ALTO, California - Intel Corp, the world's largest maker of computer chips, says it will encourage personal computer makers to advertise on the World Wide Web next year in a programme which analysts estimate could raise annual Internet advertising by roughly $250 million.

LONDON - British Digital Broadcasting says it has selected Castle Transmission International to provide the network to broadcast the 15 pay channels it will launch in the UK next year. "Over the next 12 years, BDB expects to spend approximately 200 million pounds on transmission as part of the advanced systems required to bring digital terrestrial television to people's homes," says BDB Director Nigel Walmsley.

TOKYO - Japanese electronics giant Hitachi Ltd and leading printing house Toppan Printing Co Ltd say they will jointly launch a large-scale, online visual data service in Japan in the autumn. The business will offer a variety of services, including licensing of the images, sales of CD-ROMs and DVD-ROMs, and access to a cybermuseum and a digital art gallery, Hitachi and Toppan say.

LONDON - The BBC's share of Britain's television viewing audience in the 12 months ended June 30 edged down for a second consecutive quarter, Britain's television watchdog says. The BBC 1 and BBC 2 channels together claimed 43.4 percent of the viewing audience, down from 43.9 percent in the 12 months ended March 31, the Independent Television Commission says.

NEW YORK - Time Warner Inc says it is seeking to sell seven cable television systems that it owns in the United States. The systems are located in southeastern Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee and Michigan and serve about 154,000 subscribers.
MUNICH - German television group ProSieben AG says it expects stable but slower growth in the German television advertising market.

NEW YORK - The Disney Channel has been grabbing more viewers going the basic cable route, a switch from its origins as a premium -- or pay -- programming service, and momentum is likely to build, network President Anne Sweeney says.

SEATTLE - Microsoft Corp. plans to announce that it will acquire Internet startup VXtreme Inc., industry sources say. One source familiar with the deal says that Microsoft's acquisition price values VXtreme at $75 million.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - Deutsche Telekon AG confirms it has lost national airline Lufthansa AG as a phone customer. Confirming a report in newsweekly Focus, Telekom says Lufthansa is switching over to Viag Interkom GmbH, a telecommunications venture between utility Viag AG and British Telecommunications Plc.

PITESTI, Romania - The unsophisticated Dacia car produced in Romania for nearly 30 years is still by far the most popular vehicle among consumers coping with post-communist economic hardship. The cars sell for less than $4,000 each.

TOKYO - Japan's Calpis Food Industry Co Ltd says it will form a business alliance with U.S. fruit juice producer Welch Foods Inc to produce and sell Welch's-brand juice in Japan. The companies hope the alliance will strengthen Calpis' position in the fruit juice market while boosting Welch's sales in Japan, Calpis says.

SYDNEY - Card Technologies Australia Ltd says its CiT smart card technology will be included in the Swatch Access watch, giving the watch payment access via a computer chip and antenna. The company says it has entered into a marketing agreement following the completion of development of the new watch.
PALO ALTO, California - Hewlett-Packard Co cuts list prices by up to 17 percent on its line of HP OmniBook notebook personal computers.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - British companies are tuning in to weather forecasts to help predict consumer trends in a move that is saving them millions of pounds a year. Using new methodology, the Weather Initiative can produce complex forecasts of the weather's effect on consumer demand for individual products and pinpoint the fluctuations of sales of a single brand.

LONDON - The British are Europe's largest consumers of chocolate, spending an average of $91.11 per person each year, according to a new market report. Market research group Datamonitor says the European chocolate market is worth about $18 billion annually, up from $16.84 billion in 1992.

HONG KONG - A comics craze is sweeping through Hong Kong, dominating the lives of thousands of fanatics willing to brave the elements for a good, vulgar read. Some 1,500 young comic fanatics camped overnight outside a recent book fair, getting set to rush in and snap up the pick of comics on the opening day.
